======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Sole proprietorship
======================================================================

{{Short description|Business legally synonymous with its owner}}
{{Companies law}}
A '''sole proprietorship''', also known as a '''sole tradership''', '''individual entrepreneurship''' or '''proprietorship''', is a type of enterprise [[ownership|owned]] and run by only one person and in which there is no legal distinction between the owner and the [[Types of business entity|business entity]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=What is a sole proprietorship |url=https://www.acra.gov.sg/how-to-guides/starting-sole-proprietorships/what-is-a-sole-proprietorship |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=Default |language=en}}</ref> A sole trader does not necessarily work alone and may employ other people.<ref>The Accountancy Partnership, [https://www.theaccountancy.co.uk/articles/information/can-a-sole-trader-have-employees-639.html Can a sole trader have employees?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922174150/https://www.theaccountancy.co.uk/articles/information/can-a-sole-trader-have-employees-639.html |date=2018-09-22 }} published 10 March 2012, accessed 22 September 2018</ref>

The sole trader receives all profits (subject to taxation specific to the business) and has [[unlimited liability|unlimited responsibility]] for all losses and [[Debt|debts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=What is the difference between a business being sole proprietor and a Limited Liability Company (LLC)? {{!}} Falmouth ME |url=https://www.falmouthme.org/town-clerk/faq/what-is-the-difference-between-a-business-being-sole-proprietor-and-a-limited |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=www.falmouthme.org}}</ref> Every asset of the business is owned by the proprietor, and all debts of the business are those of the proprietor; the business is not a separate [[Legal person|legal entity]]. The arrangement is a "sole" proprietorship in contrast with a [[partnership]], which has at least two owners.

Sole proprietors may use a [[trade name]] or business name other than their legal name. They may have to [[trademark]] their business name if it differs from their own legal name, with the process varying depending upon country of residence.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.smallbusiness.wa.gov.au/step-3-how-do-i-register-my-business-name/|title = Small Business.gov.au - How do I register my business name?|access-date = 2015-07-13|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140820064531/http://www.smallbusiness.wa.gov.au/step-3-how-do-i-register-my-business-name/|archive-date = 2014-08-20|url-status = dead}}</ref>

==Advantages and disadvantages==
Registration of a [[business name]] for a sole proprietor is not mandatory in many countries and is generally uncomplicated unless it involves the selection of a name that is fictitious or [[Assumed identity|assumed]]. In many countries, the business owner is required to register with the appropriate [[local authorities]], who will determine that the name submitted is not already in use by another [[business entity]].

The owner may hire [[Employment|employees]] and enlist the services of [[Independent contractor|independent consultants]]. Although an employee or consultant may be requested by the owner to complete a specific project or participate in the company's [[decision-making]] process, their contribution to the project or decision is considered a ''recommendation'' under the law. Under the [[legal doctrine]] of ''[[respondeat superior]]'' ([[Latin]]: "let the master answer"), the [[legal liability]] for any business decision arising from such a contribution remains with the owner and cannot be renounced or [[Apportionment|apportioned]].

This is offset by the unlimited liability attached to a sole proprietary business. The owner carries the financial responsibility for all debts and losses suffered by the business, to the extent of using personal or other assets to discharge any outstanding [[Liability (financial accounting)|liabilities]]. Thus, the owner of a sole proprietorship may be forced to use their personal holdings, such as their car, to pay the debts.<ref>{{cite book |title=Business |date=8 February 2016 |publisher=O. C. Ferrell, Geoffrey A. Hirt, Linda Ferrell |isbn=978-1-259-57814-4 |edition=V}}</ref> The owner is exclusively liable for all business activities conducted by the sole proprietorship and is accordingly entitled to full control and all earnings associated with it.

==Rules for sole proprietorships in various countries==
=== Netherlands===

In the Netherlands, a sole trader can be categorized as a "ZZPer", and must register with the [[Kamer van Koophandel|Chamber of Commerce]] and get a [[VAT identification number|VAT ID]].<ref>Dutch Chamber of commerce, [https://www.kvk.nl/advies-en-informatie/bedrijf-starten/starten-als-zzper-7-belangrijke-stappen/] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217130023/https://www.kvk.nl/advies-en-informatie/bedrijf-starten/starten-als-zzper-7-belangrijke-stappen/|date=2019-12-17}}, Published 12 June 2019, accessed 17 December 2019</ref> Not all ZZPers are sole traders. A ZZPer (meaning Zelfstandige Zonder Personeel or self-employed without staff) is an entrepreneur who does not employ any staff to run their business. A business can be a sole proprietorship and also employ staff in which case the entrepreneur does not qualify as a ZZPer. 

===Ireland===
In Ireland, a sole trader who wishes to trade using a business name other than their true surname must register that name with the [[Companies Registration Office (Ireland)|Companies Registration Office]] (CRO).<ref>Citizens Information Board, [http://www.citizensinformation.ie/en/employment/types_of_employment/self_employment/setting_up_a_business_in_ireland.html Starting a Business] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922173458/http://www.citizensinformation.ie/en/employment/types_of_employment/self_employment/setting_up_a_business_in_ireland.html |date=2018-09-22 }}, published 21 March 2018, accessed 22 September 2018</ref>

=== Malaysia ===
==== Registration of sole proprietorships ====
In Malaysia, there are three laws governing the registration and administration of sole proprietors:-
# West Malaysia and the Federal Territory of [[Labuan]]: Registration of Business Act 1956 (Act 197);<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ssm.com.my/sites/default/files/acts/fscommand/a0197.htm|title=Registration of Business Act 1956|website=Companies Commission of Malaysia|access-date=2018-01-16}}</ref>
# [[Sarawak]]: Businesses, Professions and Trade Licensing Ordinance [Sarawak Chapter 33];<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.betong.sarawak.gov.my/modules/web/pages.php?mod=publication&sub=publication_show&id=9|title=Business, Profession and Trade Licensing Ordinance (Sarawak Chapter 33)|website=Betong Division Website|access-date=16 January 2018}}</ref> and Business Names Ordinance for the State of Sarawak [Sarawak Chapter 64]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.betong.sarawak.gov.my/modules/web/pages.php?mod=publication&sub=publication_show&id=8|title=Sarawak Business Names Ordinance|website=Betong Division Website|access-date=16 January 2018}}</ref> and
# [[Sabah]]: Trades Licensing Ordinance for the State of Sabah [Sabah Chapter 144].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lawnet.sabah.gov.my/Lawnet/SabahLawsDeclaredFederal/TradesLicensingOrdinance(SabahCap144).pdf|title=Trades Licensing Ordinance [Sabah Chapter 144]|website=Sabah State Attorney-General's Chambers}}</ref>
In West Malaysia, the registration of sole proprietors come under the purview of the [[Companies Commission of Malaysia]] (''Suruhanjaya Syarikat Malaysia'', abbreviated as ''SSM''). In Sabah and Sarawak (with the exception of [[Kuching]]), the registrations of businesses are done at the local authorities (e.g. municipal councils or district offices), while in Kuching, sole proprietors are registered with the Kuching Office of the Malaysian Inland Revenue Board.

Sole proprietors, which includes the self-employed, must register with the relevant authority within thirty days from the commencement of their business.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ssm.com.my/sites/default/files/guidelines/OWNER%20RESPONSIBILITY_new.pdf|title=Responsibility of Business Owner|website=Companies Commission of Malaysia|access-date=16 January 2018}}</ref> Sole proprietors may register their business using one of two names: their legal name following the registrant's identity card or a trade name.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ssm.com.my/en/sole/starting-a-sole-proprietorship-partnership|title=Starting a Sole Proprietorship/Partnership|website=Companies Commission of Malaysia|date=9 May 2011 |access-date=16 January 2018}}</ref> Registration of a business lasts for either one or two years, and must be renewed thirty days before its expiry.<ref name=":0" />

In the event of termination of business, the proprietor has thirty days from the termination date to file the notice with the relevant authority.<ref name=":0" /> If the termination is caused by the death of the proprietor, the administrators of the estate have four months from the death date to file a notice of termination.<ref name=":0" />

==== Goods and services tax (GST) ====
Sole proprietors must register with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department to charge and collect goods and services tax (GST) once their taxable turnover within a 12 month-period exceeds RM500,000.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gst.customs.gov.my/en/SiteAssets/doc/Registering%20for%20GST%20Amend%201.pdf|title=Getting Ready for GST – Registering for GST|website=Royal Malaysian Customs Department|access-date=16 January 2018}}</ref>

==== Sole proprietors as employers ====
Similar to other Common Law jurisdiction, proprietors may enter into contracts of employment and/or apprenticeship with their employees. Sole proprietors, as employers are responsible to:
* Make contribution to their employees' Employees Provident Fund;<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kwsp.gov.my/portal/en/employers|title=EPF - Employers - KWSP|website=www.kwsp.gov.my|language=ms-MY|access-date=2018-01-16}}</ref> and
* Pay contribution to their employees' Social Security.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.perkeso.gov.my/index.php/en/social-security-protection/employer-employee-eligibility|title=Employer & Employee Eligibility|website=www.perkeso.gov.my|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-01-16}}</ref>

==== Online businesses ====
In 2016, the SSM took legal action against 478 online businesses that had failed to register, whether as sole proprietors, partnerships, or private limited companies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2016/01/26/ssm-unregistered-businesses-cannot-sell-products-online/|title=SSM: Unregistered businesses cannot sell products online - Nation {{!}} The Star Online|website=www.thestar.com.my|date=26 January 2016 |access-date=2018-01-16}}</ref> As at May 12, 2017, a total of 50,882 online businesses have registered with the SSM since 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.astroawani.com/berita-bisnes/50-882-peniaga-online-berdaftar-dengan-ssm-143421|title=50882 peniaga online berdaftar dengan SSM|website=www.astroawani.com|date=21 May 2017 |language=ms|access-date=2018-01-16}}</ref>

===New Zealand===
Sole traders in New Zealand must notify the [[Inland Revenue Department (New Zealand)|Inland Revenue Department]] that they are trading and must register for [[Goods and Services Tax (New Zealand)|Goods and Services Tax]] purposes if their income exceeds $60,000 per year.<ref>New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, [https://www.business.govt.nz/getting-started/choosing-the-right-business-structure/becoming-a-sole-trader/ Becoming a sole trader] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190121230536/https://www.business.govt.nz/getting-started/choosing-the-right-business-structure/becoming-a-sole-trader/ |date=2019-01-21 }}, accessed 25 December 2018</ref> Sole traders may obtain a unique New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), which any business in New Zealand can use to identify the business in commercial relationships and dealings with the government.<ref>[https://www.nzbn.govt.nz/get-an-nzbn/get-your-nzbn Get your NZBN] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225130029/https://www.nzbn.govt.nz/get-an-nzbn/get-your-nzbn |date=2018-12-25 }}, accessed 25 December 2018</ref>

===United Kingdom ===
A sole trader is the simplest type of business structure defined in UK law. It refers to an individual who owns their own business and retains all the profits from it. When starting up, sole traders must complete a straightforward registration with [[HM Revenue and Customs]] as self-employed for tax and [[National Insurance]] purposes. They are responsible for maintaining the business's records and submitting an annual tax return for all income from self-employment and other work.<ref>Business Link, [http://www.businesslink.gov.uk/bdotg/action/detail?itemId=1073789606&type=RESOURCES  Legal Structures: The Basics - Sole Trader] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015093518/http://www.businesslink.gov.uk/bdotg/action/detail?itemId=1073789606&type=RESOURCES |date=2012-10-15 }}</ref> If revenue is expected to be more than £85,000 a year, they must also register for [[Value-added tax in the United Kingdom|Value Added Tax]]. A sole trader can employ staff, but is personally responsible for any losses the business takes.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Set up as self-employed (a 'sole trader'): step by step |url=https://www.gov.uk/set-up-self-employed |access-date=2023-02-06 |website=GOV.UK |language=en}}</ref>

==== Advantages ====
Becoming a sole trader is relatively simple compared to other business structures. It can rapidly enable a business to begin trading; the requirements for record-keeping are far more straightforward than other business structures. Sole traders make all operational decisions and are solely responsible for raising business finance. They can invest their own capital into the business, or may be able to access business loans and/or overdrafts. Unlike limited companies or partnerships, it is not necessary to share decision-making or the profits.<ref name=":1" />

==== Disadvantages ====
Unlike many other business entities, the sole proprietorship lacks a clear distinction between personal and business income.<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Mirrlees |editor1-first=James |title=Tax by design : the Mirrlees review |date=2011 |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford |isbn=9780198816386 |page=451}}</ref> The business owner is personally liable for income tax and National Insurance contributions due on the business profits in each tax year. They are also personally liable for any debts the business incurs. Business analysts may advise sole traders to form a [[limited company]] in order to access greater levels of financing, for example for expansion plans. This can limit their personal liability, and business lenders may be more inclined to co-operate with a limited company. It can also be the case that within certain industries, it is easier to secure work if presenting potential business partners with a limited company structure.

===United States===
In the United States, there are no formalities that must be followed to start a sole proprietorship or commence business as a sole proprietor. However, depending upon the business activity of the sole proprietorship, sole proprietors may require licenses and permits in order to conduct business.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Carter|first1=Christopher|title=What Are the Registration Requirements & Procedures for Sole Proprietorship?|url=http://smallbusiness.chron.com/registration-requirements-procedures-sole-proprietorship-3953.html|website=Chron|publisher=Texas Chronicle|access-date=26 January 2018}}</ref>

According to the [[Small Business Administration]] (SBA), a sole proprietor and their business are considered as one and the same; therefore, the business is not subjected to separate taxation and regarded as the direct income of the owner. Income, losses and expenses may be listed on a Schedule C, which is then transferred to the personal tax return of the owner.<ref name="proprietorshipsIRS">{{cite web|title=Sole Proprietorships|url=https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/sole-proprietorships|website=IRS|publisher=Internal Revenue Service|access-date=26 January 2018|date=14 December 2017}}</ref> It is the responsibility of the owner to ensure all due income taxes and self-employment contributions are paid.

A permitted exception to the sole proprietor (single owner) stipulation is made by the [[Internal Revenue Service]] (IRS) permitting the spouse of a sole proprietor to work for the business. They are not classified as partners in the enterprise, or an [[independent contractor]], enabling the business to retain its sole proprietorship status and not be required to submit a partnership income tax return.<ref>{{cite web|title=Husband and Wife Business|url=https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/husband-and-wife-business|website=Internal Revenue Service|publisher=irs.gov|access-date=8 September 2016}}</ref> If an individual elects to incorporate as a [[Limited liability company]] but elects to be taxed as a [[Corporation]], the IRS no longer recognizes the individual as a sole proprietorship.<ref name="proprietorshipsIRS"/>

====Foundation and development====
The setting-up process of a sole proprietorship to comply with local laws and regulations, is obtainable from the Small Business Development Center (SBDC), using their locator facility. A sole proprietor must be prepared to devote their time, utilizing business methods towards establishing a sound and appropriate foundation. Doing so may contribute to increased turnover, profits, minimize taxes, and avoid other potential adversities.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Weltman|first1=Barbara|title=J.K. Lasser's Small Business Taxes 2011: Your Complete Guide to a Better|date=2011|publisher=Wiley|isbn=978-0470939574|url=https://archive.org/details/jklasserssmallbu0000welt|url-access=registration|access-date=26 January 2018}}</ref>

Sole owners are engaged in many varieties of industry and commerce, and a comprehensive list of the primary categories is found in the [[North American Industry Classification System]] (NAICS). The selection of a business type, by a new sole proprietor, is in many instances, motivated by appropriate business experience in a particular field, especially those pertaining to enterprises involving the marketing and selling of defined products and services.

A crucial component of a sole proprietorship within a business plan is the provision of an inherent guideline, for actions that require implementing for a business to achieve growth. The business name and products are critical aspects in the founding of a sole proprietorship and once selected, should be protected. In the event of a determined brand name being legalized, information regarding trademark protection is available from the [[U.S. Patent and Trademark Office]].

====Finance====
For the sole proprietor, there are a variety of options in obtaining financial support for their business, including loan facilities available from the U.S. [[Small Business Administration]]. The loans are not originated by the SBA, but the administration does guarantee loans made by various independent lending institutions. The primary loan facility for small businesses offered by this agency is the 7(a) loan program, designed for general applications.<ref>{{cite web|title = 7(a) Loan Program|url = https://www.sba.gov/7a-loan-program|website = SBA.gov|access-date = 11 December 2014}}</ref> Sole proprietors are able to finance legitimate operating expenses; for example, working capital, furniture, leasehold improvements and building renovations.

Many and varied private organizations and individuals seek opportunities to invest and fund a business that may not qualify for [[Small business financing|traditional financing]] from institutions, such as banks. For the sole proprietor seeking to take advantage of this facility, there are various factors that must be understood and adhered to regarding the loan application.

The Small Business Administration (SBA) advises that there are traditionally two forms of financing: [[debt]] and [[Equity (finance)|equity]]. For any small business owner seeking funding, they must consider the [[debt-to-equity ratio]] of their enterprise.<ref>{{cite web|title=The SBA Loan Guarantee Program|url=https://www.sba.gov/sites/default/files/SDOLoanFactSheet_Oct_2011.pdf|website=Small Business Administration|access-date=26 January 2018|date=October 2011}}</ref>

According to the SBA, there are various private organizations prepared to fund sole proprietor business operations that do not qualify for traditional financing from banks. These private investors can provide loans, credit lines, leasing facilities for equipment, or other forms of capital, to sole proprietorships that have exhausted alternative financial resources. It is also possible for these owners to obtain financing by way of [[business partners]] or others, with cash to invest. Financial partners are frequently "silent" and although they do not participate in any business related decisions, they generally receive a percentage of the profits, generated by the business.

To assist sole proprietors, there are business grants available from the Federal Government or private organizations, providing certain criteria are met. To qualify for Federal grants,<ref>{{cite web|title = Sole Proprietorship Loan Programs|url = http://www.sba.gov/category/navigation-structure/loans-grants/small-business-loans/sba-loan-programs|website = SBA.gov|access-date = 11 December 2014}}</ref> small businesses must comply with determined business size and income standards. For consideration regarding various grant opportunities, sole proprietors may apply for a grant in their capacity as an individual. Local governments and state economic development agencies frequently make grants available, for businesses that stimulate their local economies.

For any sole proprietor applying for a loan, before starting the loan procedure, it is essential that their personal and business credit history is in order and up-to-date. A personal credit report should be obtained from a credit bureau; for example, Trans-Union, [[Equifax]] or [[Experian]]. This action should be initiated by a business owner well before starting the borrowing process. The Small Business Administration specifies that all credit reports received from any source should be carefully reviewed to ensure that all relevant personal information is correct. Other content in the report should also be examined particularly that related to the past credit obtained, from sources such as credit cards, mortgages, and student loans, as well as details pertaining to how the credit was repaid.

===Other countries ===
An exact equivalent of "sole proprietorship" is often absent, because the focus of the concept can change. An example is the Brazilian concept of "sole business" that was split into two main kinds of [[Freelancer|formal freelancer]]:
*'''sole professional''': with [[Academic certificate#Higher-level academic certificates|higher level academic certificate]] and regulations for formal control of autonomous exercise (e.g. sole doctor's office)
*'''sole entrepreneur''': "little entrepreneurs", such as a craftsman, autonomous taxi driver, and many others, that can be formal. An informal freelancer, through a simple process, can be formalized as ''sole microentrepreneur.''

[[Taxation in Germany|German]] and [[Law of Austria|Austrian]] tax laws also differentiate between sole professionals and other sole proprietors.

'''Sridhar R. Tayur''' is an American business professor, entrepreneur, and management thinker.<ref name="tayur-atlantic" /><ref>{{cite web | url=https://cen.cornell.edu/spotlight | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130420010933/http://cen.cornell.edu/spotlight | url-status=dead | archive-date=April 20, 2013 | title=Cornell Entrepreneur Spotlight | publisher=Cornell.edu | access-date=November 12, 2014  }}</ref> He is university professor of operations management and Ford Distinguished Research Chair at the [[Tepper School of Business]], [[Carnegie Mellon University]], and the founder of SmartOps Corporation <ref>{{cite news | first=Ron | last=Wilcox | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/case-in-point-how-close-can-you-stand-to-a-software-giant/2011/06/20/AG9OjskH_story.html|title=How close can you stand to a software giant? | date=June 25, 2011 | newspaper=The Washington Post | access-date= 9 September 2012}}</ref><ref name=ppg-st-story-1>{{cite news | first=T. F. | last=Lindeman | url=https://www.post-gazette.com/businessnews/2003/08/28/New-Pittsburgh-Well-funded-SmartOps-helping-firms-with-supply-chain-management/stories/200308280016|title=New Pittsburgh: Well-funded SmartOps helping firms with supply chain management | date=Aug 28, 2003 | newspaper= Pittsburgh Post-Gazette | url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140516025634/https://www.post-gazette.com/business/businessnews/2003/08/28/New-Pittsburgh-Well-funded-SmartOps-helping-firms-with-supply-chain-management/stories/200308280016 |archive-date=May 16, 2014}}</ref> and OrganJet Corporation.<ref name="hbs-organjet">{{cite web|url=http://hbr.org/product/organjet-and-guardianwings/an/413068-PDF-ENG|title=Harvard Business School Case 413-068: "OrganJet and GuardianWings" by Julie Battilana and James Weber|date=27 February 2013|publisher=Harvard Business School|access-date=8 November 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scienceofbetter.org/podcast/tayur.html|title=Speed transplants, save lives|date=27 May 2011|publisher=scienceofbetter.org|access-date=9 September 2012}}</ref>

Tayur is known as an "academic capitalist,"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cmu.edu/50/founder-stories/story-tayur.html|title=Founder: Sridhar Tayur – 50 Years as Carnegie Mellon University – Carnegie Mellon University|last=Carnegie Mellon University|website=www.cmu.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-05-01}}</ref> recognized for his contribution to [[inventory theory|Inventory Theory]],<ref name="gsk-st" /> [[Supply Chain Management]], [[Lean Manufacturing]], Operations Strategy,<ref>{{cite web |url= http://hstalks.com/?t=MM1623488-Tayur |title= Caterpillar bundles to win: operations strategy in action |last1= Tayur |first1= S. |year= 2012 |work= Operations Strategy, The Marketing & Management Collection | editor-last = Van Mieghem | editor-first = J.A. |publisher=Henry Stewart Talks Ltd |location= London |access-date=13 December 2012}}</ref> [[Healthcare]] Management, and [[Quantum computing|Quantum Computing]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cmu.edu/tepper/faculty-and-research/research/quantum-computing-business.html|title=Quantum Computing Uses to Solve Problems in Business – Tepper School of Business – Carnegie Mellon University|last=University|first=Carnegie Mellon|website=www.cmu.edu|language=en|access-date=2019-11-25}}</ref> He describes his own work as "research, industrial implementation, [[software entrepreneurship]], investing in start-ups and turnarounds, and creating a social enterprise" that lies "in the intersection of math, money, and morals."<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tayur|first=Sridhar|date=2017-09-22|title=OM Forum—An Essay on Operations Management|journal=Manufacturing & Service Operations Management|volume=19|issue=4|pages=526–533|doi=10.1287/msom.2017.0665|issn=1523-4614|doi-access=free}}</ref> Tayur's work "has earned him a reputation as someone uniquely talented in identifying, and then solving, novel and timely problems confronting society," according to a 2014 [[Production and Operations Management|''Productions and Operations Management'']] article honoring him.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Sridhar Tayur|journal=Production and Operations Management|volume=23|issue=5|year=2014|pages=xi–xii|issn=1059-1478|doi=10.1111/poms.12145}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Tayur attended [[Hyderabad Public School]], Begumpet, an elite school in the state of [[Telangana]]. He earned his [[Bachelor of Technology|B. Tech]] in [[Mechanical Engineering]] from [[Indian Institute of Technology Madras|IIT Madras]] in 1986<ref name="iitm.ac.in">Chennai36: [http://chennai36.iitm.ac.in/do-whatever-you-like-to-do-but-do-something-a-talk-with-professor-sridhar-tayur/ Do whatever you like to do, but do something: A talk with Professor Sridhar Tayur | Chennai36], accessdate: May 14, 2016</ref> and [[Ph.D.]] in operations research and [[industrial engineering]] from [[Cornell University|Cornell]] in 1990.

He joined [[Carnegie Mellon University|Carnegie Mellon]] in 1991 as an assistant professor in [[Tepper School of Business|The Graduate School of Industrial Administration (GSIA)]] (today known as Tepper School of Business), obtained tenure in 1996, and was promoted to full professor in 1998. In 2019, he was appointed to university professor, the highest designation a faculty member can receive at Carnegie Mellon.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cmu.edu/tepper/news/stories/2019/may/sridhar-tayur-university-professor.html|title=Tepper School Faculty Sridhar Tayur Named University Professor – Tepper School of Business – Carnegie Mellon University|last=University|first=Carnegie Mellon|date=2019-05-04|website=www.cmu.edu|language=en|access-date=2019-05-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cmu.edu/faculty-office/university-prof/index.html|title=University Professors – Vice Provost for Faculty – Carnegie Mellon University|last=University|first=Carnegie Mellon|website=www.cmu.edu|language=en|access-date=2019-05-01}}</ref> He holds Ford Distinguished Research Chair in Operations Management. Within Carnegie Mellon, he holds courtesy appointments in the [[Heinz College]] and [[Carnegie Mellon College of Engineering|Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ece.cmu.edu/directory/courtesy-faculty.html|title=Courtesy faculty – Electrical and Computer Engineering – College of Engineering – Carnegie Mellon University|last=Carnegie Mellon University|website=www.ece.cmu.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-07-06}}</ref> He has held a courtesy appointment as professor of [[cardiology]] (2009–2011) at the Gerald McGinnis Center of [[West Penn Allegheny Health System]].<ref name="wafarin">{{Cite journal | last1 = Radhakrishnan | first1 = A. | last2 = Vido | first2 = D. | last3 = Tayur | first3 = S. | last4 = Akan | first4 = M. | last5 = Murali | first5 = S. | title = Genotype Guided Therapeutic Dosing of Warfarin in Geriatric Patients | doi = 10.1016/S0735-1097(12)61697-0 | journal = Journal of the American College of Cardiology | volume = 59 | issue = 13 | pages = E1696 | year = 2012 | doi-access = free }}</ref> Tayur has held visiting positions at [[Cornell University]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and [[Stanford University]].

Tayur was president (2001–2002) of the Manufacturing and Service Operations Management Society (MSOM),<ref>[http://msom.society.informs.org/minutes/01FMiamiMinutes.html MSOM Business Meeting Minutes, INFORMS Fall Conference, November 5, 2001 (Miami)]</ref> one of the largest societies of the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]] (INFORMS). He has served on the editorial boards of [[Management Science (journal)|''Management Science'']], [[Operations Research (journal)|''Operations Research'']], ''[[Manufacturing & Service Operations Management]]'', ''IIE Transactions'', ''Optimization and Engineering'', and [[Production and Operations Management|''Productions and Operations Management'']], among others, and he is a department editor at [[Management Science (journal)|''Management Science'']], for the Entrepreneurship and Innovation Department.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pubsonline.informs.org/page/mnsc/editorial-board|title=Management Science: INFORMS|website=pubsonline.informs.org|language=en|access-date=2018-01-06}}</ref>

Tayur founded SmartOps (in 2000) and OrganJet (in 2011), and has consulted for various organizations, including [[Caterpillar Inc.|Caterpillar]],<ref name="ppg-st-story-1" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shunko|first1=Masha|last2=Yunes|first2=Tallys|last3=Fenu|first3=Giulio|last4=Scheller-Wolf|first4=Alan|last5=Tardif|first5=Valerie|last6=Tayur|first6=Sridhar|title=Product Portfolio Restructuring: Methodology and Application at Caterpillar|journal=Production and Operations Management|volume=27|language=en|pages=100–120|doi=10.1111/poms.12786|issn=1937-5956|year=2018}}</ref> [[ConAgra Foods]],<ref name="tayur interfaces 12" /> [[Deere & Company|Deere]],<ref name="deereinfoworld">{{cite journal |author=Schwartz, E. |year=2005 |title= Supply-chain victory |journal=  InfoWorld |volume=27 |issue=17 |pages=12 |id={{ProQuest|194360091}} }}</ref> [[Kenn Ricci#Flight Options|Flight Options]],<ref name="tayur interfaces 12" /> [[General Electric]],<ref name="ppg-st-story-1" /> [[GlaxoSmithKline]],<ref name="gsk-st">{{cite web | url=https://public.tepper.cmu.edu/Faculty/Tayur/cd/success.htm | title=The Academy of Logistics: Successful Inventory Planning Requires a New Approach | publisher = Tepper.cmu.edu | date = October 2002 | access-date = December 29, 2014   }}</ref> [[Intel]],<ref name="ppg-st-story-1" /> [[Kellogg's]],<ref name="tayur interfaces 12" /> and [[Microsoft]].<ref name="in-game-scheduling">{{Cite journal | last1 = Turner | first1 = J. | last2 = Scheller-Wolf | first2 = A. | last3 = Tayur | first3 = S. | title = OR PRACTICE--Scheduling of Dynamic In-Game Advertising | doi = 10.1287/opre.1100.0852 | journal = Operations Research | volume = 59 | pages = 1–16 | year = 2011 }}</ref> Tayur has also served as a "consultant to the firm" for [[McKinsey & Company]] in the areas of [[lean manufacturing]] and [[supply chain management]].

== Academic work ==

=== Research ===
Tayur's work covers various [[operations management]] fields, including [[supply chain management]], [[lean manufacturing]], and [[healthcare]]. His papers have been published in [[Operations Research (journal)|''Operations Research'']], [[Management Science (journal)|''Management Science'']], ''[[Manufacturing & Service Operations Management]]'', ''[[Mathematics of Operations Research]]'', ''[[Mathematical Programming]]'', ''[[Queueing Systems]]'', ''IIE Transactions'', and ''[[Production and Operations Management]],'' among others. Notable collaborators include INFORMS Fellows such as [[Dimitris Bertsimas]], Paul Glasserman, Jack Muckstadt, [[Georgia Perakis]], and Robin Roundy (his Ph.D. thesis advisor); faculty colleagues Alan Scheller-Wolf, R. Ravi (INFORMS Fellow), and [[Ravindran Kannan]]; and Ph.D. students Srinagesh Gavirneni, Roman Kapuscinski, [[Pınar Keskinocak]] (INFORMS Fellow), and Jay Swaminathan (INFORMS Fellow). He is recognized for his operations research work in developing novel algorithms for models in stochastic [[inventory theory]] (using Infinitesimal Perturbation Analysis).<ref name="CroninLoewenstein2018">{{cite book|author1=Matthew A. Cronin|author2=Jeffrey Loewenstein|title=The Craft of Creativity|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gEwdtAEACAAJ|year=2018|publisher=Stanford University Press|isbn=978-0-8047-8737-6}}</ref>

'''Manufacturing, Retail and Supply Chain.''' Tayur developed Infinitesimal Perturbation Analysis (IPA) for stochastic inventory models, with a wide number of applications, including managing product variety using vanilla boxes, designing rapid-response supply chains, and omni-channel retailing.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Glasserman|first1=Paul|last2=Tayur|first2=Sridhar|date=1995-02-01|title=Sensitivity Analysis for Base-Stock Levels in Multiechelon Production-Inventory Systems|url=http://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/abs/10.1287/mnsc.41.2.263|journal=Management Science|language=en|volume=41|issue=2|pages=263–281|doi=10.1287/mnsc.41.2.263|issn=0025-1909|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Swaminathan|first1=Jayashankar M.|last2=Tayur|first2=Sridhar R.|date=1998-12-01|title=Managing Broader Product Lines through Delayed Differentiation Using Vanilla Boxes|url=http://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/abs/10.1287/mnsc.44.12.S161|journal=Management Science|language=en|volume=44|issue=12–part–2|pages=S161–S172|doi=10.1287/mnsc.44.12.S161|issn=0025-1909|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="tayurfortune" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Jia|first1=Su|last2=Karp|first2=Jeremy|last3=Ravi|first3=R.|last4=Tayur|first4=Sridhar|date=2021-12-01|title=Effective Online Order Acceptance Policies for Omnichannel Fulfillment|url=http://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/msom.2021.1024|journal=Manufacturing & Service Operations Management|volume=24 |issue=3 |language=en|pages=1650–1663|doi=10.1287/msom.2021.1024|s2cid=244831869|issn=1523-4614|url-access=subscription}}</ref> His 2021 [[National Science Foundation]] Distinguished Lecture, jointly sponsored by the Directorates of Engineering (ENG), Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE), and Mathematics and Physical Sciences (MPS), summarized his work on responsive and resilient supply chains using novel quantum and classical algorithms. In addition, he has examined the "dark side" of [[Global supply chain governance|global supply chains]], including [[counterfeiting]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cho |first1=Soo-Haeng |last2=Fang |first2=Xin |last3=Tayur |first3=Sridhar |date=2015 |title=Combating Strategic Counterfeiters in Licit and Illicit Supply Chains |url=http://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/msom.2015.0524 |journal=Manufacturing & Service Operations Management |language=en |volume=17 |issue=3 |pages=273–289 |doi=10.1287/msom.2015.0524 |s2cid=10058833 |issn=1523-4614|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[child labour]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cho |first1=Soo-Haeng |last2=Fang |first2=Xin |last3=Tayur |first3=Sridhar |last4=Xu |first4=Ying |date=2019 |title=Combating Child Labor: Incentives and Information Disclosure in Global Supply Chains |url=http://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/msom.2018.0733 |journal=Manufacturing & Service Operations Management |language=en |volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=692–711 |doi=10.1287/msom.2018.0733 |issn=1523-4614|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

[[File:Tayur-Roth-WH-16.jpg|thumb|Tayur with [[Alvin E. Roth]] at the White House Summit on Organ Donation (June 2016)]]
'''Healthcare Analytics, Operations, and Policy.''' At [[Allegheny General Hospital]], Tayur has conducted clinical trials that have established the clinical benefits of genotype guided therapeutic dosing of warfarin therapy.<ref name="wafarin" /> Tayur's work with Dr. [[Bennet Omalu]], whose discovery of [[chronic traumatic encephalopathy]] (CTE) was featured in the movie [[Concussion (2015 film)|''Concussion'']],<ref>{{cite news |last=Belson |first=Ken |url=http://mobile.nytimes.com/2015/09/02/sports/football/makers-of-sonys-concussion-film-tried-to-avoid-angering-nfl-emails-show.html?post_id=10152838169215474_10153022912360474#_=_ |title=Sony Altered 'Concussion' Film to Prevent N.F.L. Protests, Emails Show |work=The New York Times |date=2015-09-01 |access-date=2015-09-02 }}</ref> applies OM methods to improve Medical Examiner Offices.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1177/097206340700900105| title = Forecasting as an Operations Management Tool in a Medical Examiner's Office| journal = Journal of Health Management| volume = 9| pages = 75–84| year = 2007| last1 = Omalu | first1 = B. I.| last2 = Shakir | first2 = A. M.| last3 = Lindner | first3 = J. L.| last4 = Tayur | first4 = S. R.| s2cid = 73325253}}</ref> In the area of [[long-term care]], Tayur has examined ways to improve the consistency of staffing and proposed an "[[On call shift|on-call]] pool" approach.<ref>{{Citation|last=Vincent Slaugh|title=Consistent Staffing for Long-Term Care Through On-Call Pools|date=2016-05-24|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mUc_LyTd730|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref>

To address the fundamental problem of scarcity of supply of organs, Tayur has collaborated with the New Jersey Sharing Network and Nevada Donor Network, among other [[organ procurement organization]]s (OPOs), to investigate [[Behavioral economics|behavioral]] approaches that will increase the consent rate from legal [[next of kin]] (NOK) of deceased individuals through video intervention.<ref>{{Citation|title=NJSN NoK Video| date=4 January 2016 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D2R2dt51ZgA|language=en|access-date=2021-07-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite work attracted the attention of the White House [[Office of Science and Technology Policy]]<ref>{{cite web | url= Announces Key Actions to Reduce the Organ Waiting List  | via= [[NARA|National Archives]]  | author= The White House Office of the Press Secretary  }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= | date = April 2016 }}</ref> and was featured at the 24th Association for Multicultural Affairs in Transplantation Annual Meeting in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E2_GOAFAxh8|title=Nudge Presentation – AMAT – September 29,2016|date=September 29, 2016|website=Youtube.com|access-date=November 7, 2016}}</ref> He has studied various aspects of split liver transplantation, including ethics,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kim|first1=Tae Wan|last2=Roberts|first2=John|last3=Strudler|first3=Alan|last4=Tayur|first4=Sridhar|date=2021-07-09|title=Ethics of split liver transplantation: should a large liver always be split if medically learning,<ref>{{Cite ssrn|last1=Tang|first1=Yanhan|last2=Scheller-Wolf|first2=Alan Andrew|last3=Tayur|first3=Sridhar R.|date=2021|title=Generalized Bandits with Learning and Queueing in Split Liver Transplantation|ssrn=3855206|ssrn-access=free}}</ref> and decisions support to determine optimal splitting policy,<ref>{{Cite ssrn|last1=Tang|first1=Yanhan (Savannah)|last2=Scheller-Wolf|first2=Alan Andrew|last3=Tayur|first3=Sridhar R.|last4=Perito|first4=Emily|last5=Roberts|first5=John P.|date=2021-06-30|title=Split Liver Transplantation: An Analytical Decision Support Model |ssrn=3877523|ssrn-access=free}}</ref> in collaboration with [[University of California, San Francisco]] transplant surgeons. His research on geographic disparity, gender inequity and video nudge were discussed at the [[National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine]] Committee on "A Fairer and More Equitable, Cost-Effective, and Transparent System of Donor Organ Procurement, Allocation, and Distribution."<ref>{{Cite web|title=A Fairer and More Equitable, Cost-Effective, and Transparent System of Donor Organ Procurement, Allocation, and Distribution: Virtual Public Listening Session|url=https://www.nationalacademies.org/event/07-15-2021/a-fairer-and-more-equitable-cost-effective-and-transparent-system-of-donor-organ-procurement-allocation-and-distribution-virtual-public-listening-session|access-date=2021-07-19|website=www.nationalacademies.org}}</ref>

Tayur supports finding other innovative methods to increase organ donation and supports the need for clarification to be able to conduct further research.[https://cartwright.house.gov/sites/cartwright.house.gov/files/Organ%20Donor%20Clarification%20Act%20FINAL.pdf] Tayur has engaged other researchers, transplant surgeons, and policy bodies, as well as students, by serving on the organizing committee of the 2016 Johns Hopkins Symposium on Healthcare Operations, with a theme of "When [[Organ transplantation|Organ Transplantation]] meets [[Operations research|Operations Research]]," and by speaking on "Effective and Innovative Solutions to Increase [[Organ donation|Organ Donation]]" at the [[Effective altruism|Harvard Effective Altruist Chapter]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/events/1069371579851112/|title=Effective and Innovative Solutions to Increase Organ Donation|website=www.facebook.com|access-date=2016-10-15}}</ref>

Tayur has studied [[Personalized medicine|personalized treatment]] for [[opioid use disorder]], specifically, the efficacy of using [[Wearable computer|wearables]] to prevent [[relapse]].<ref>{{Cite ssrn|last1=Tayur|first1=Sridhar R.|last2=Scheller-Wolf|first2=Alan Andrew|last3=Gan|first3=Kyra|date=2019-05-16|title=Personalized Treatment for Opioid Use Disorder|language=en|ssrn=3389539}}</ref>

In collaboration with the [[University of Pittsburgh Medical Center]], Tayur developed machine learning algorithms to predict hospital re-admissions due to sickle-cell disease.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Patel|first1=Arisha|last2=Gan|first2=Kyra|last3=Li|first3=Andrew A.|last4=Weiss|first4=Jeremy|last5=Nouraie|first5=Mehdi|last6=Tayur|first6=Sridhar|last7=Novelli|first7=Enrico M.|date=2021-01-01|title=Machine-learning algorithms for predicting hospital re-admissions in sickle cell disease|journal=British Journal of Haematology|volume=192|issue=1|pages=158–170|doi=10.1111/bjh.17107|issn=1365-2141|pmid=33169861|s2cid=226295279|doi-access=free|pmc=11423862 }}</ref>

In addition to his applied work, Tayur has adopted a strategic queueing approach to investigate (1) physicians' diagnostic test-ordering behavior in outpatient settings<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.poms.org/POMS%20Chronicle%20Vol%2019%20No%201.pdf|title=POMS Chronicle|date=2012|publisher=Production and Operations Management Society|volume=9|number=1|access-date=September 14, 2015}}</ref> and (2) the effect of multi-listing—powered by affordable jet services (OrganJet)—on U.S. organ transplantation candidates' life expectancy and organ wastage.<ref name="AtaSkaro2016">{{cite journal|last2=Skaro|first2=Anton|last3=Tayur|first3=Sridhar|year=2016|title=OrganJet: Overcoming Geographical Disparities in Access to Deceased Donor Kidneys in the United States|journal=Management Science|volume=63|issue=9|pages=2776–2794|doi=10.1287/mnsc.2016.2487|issn=0025-1909|last1=Ata|first1=Barış|s2cid=32489741}}</ref> Tayur has also analyzed [[Combinatorial modelling|combinatorial models]] (using quantum- and quantum-inspired algorithms) and conducted [[topological data analysis]] (using [[algebraic topology]]) to study [[cancer genomics]], using data on [[acute myeloid leukemia]] and [[Glioblastoma Multiforme]] from [[The Cancer Genome Atlas]].<ref name="denovo-st">{{cite bioRxiv|last1=Alghassi|first1=Hedayat|last2=Dridi|first2=Raouf|last3=Robertson|first3=A. Gordon|last4=Tayur|first4=Sridhar|date=2019-11-17|title=Quantum and Quantum-inspired Methods for de novo Discovery of Altered Cancer Pathways |biorxiv=10.1101/845719}}</ref><ref>{{cite bioRxiv|last1=Dridi|first1=Raouf|last2=Alghassi|first2=Hedayat|last3=Obeidat|first3=Maen|last4=Tayur|first4=Sridhar|date=2019-11-30|title=The Topology of Mutated Driver Pathways |biorxiv=10.1101/860676}}</ref>

Tayur has explored improved data-driven methods towards making Liquid Biopsy practical.<ref>{{Cite SSRN|last1=Gan|first1=Kyra|last2=Jia|first2=Su|last3=Li|first3=Andrew|last4=Tayur|first4=Sridhar R.|date=2021|title=Toward a Liquid Biopsy: Greedy Approximation Algorithmsfor Active Sequential Hypothesis Testing|ssrn=3894600|ssrn-access=free}}</ref>

'''New Business Models.''' Tayur's research has analyzed new business models such as scheduling of [[Fractional ownership of aircraft|fractional jets]],<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1287/trsc.32.3.277| title = Scheduling of Time-Shared Jet Aircraft| journal = Transportation Science| volume = 32| issue = 3| pages = 277| year = 1998| last1 = Keskinocak | first1 = P. | last2 = Tayur | first2 = S. | citeseerx = 10.1.1.25.9346}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1007/s10479-007-0274-1| title = Aircraft and crew scheduling for fractional ownership programs| journal = Annals of Operations Research| volume = 159| pages = 415–431| year = 2007| last1 = Yang | first1 = W. | last2 = Karaesmen | first2 = I. R. Z. | last3 = Keskinocak | first3 = P. N. | last4 = Tayur | first4 = S. | s2cid = 35970963}}</ref> online rental models,<ref name="SlaughBiller2016">{{cite journal|last1=Slaugh|first1=Vincent W.|last2=Biller|first2=Bahar|last3=Tayur|first3=Sridhar R.|title=Managing Rentals with Usage-Based Loss|journal=Manufacturing & Service Operations Management|volume=18|issue=3|year=2016|pages=429–444|issn=1523-4614|doi=10.1287/msom.2016.0576|citeseerx=10.1.1.703.2571}}</ref> [[online to offline]] (O2O) platforms,<ref>{{Cite ssrn|last1=Tayur|first1=Sridhar R.|last2=Li|first2=Hui|last3=Xu|first3=Joseph|date=2019-09-07|title=Online-to-Offline Platform Models|ssrn=3449744|language=en}}</ref> dynamic scheduling of advertisements in video games,<ref name="in-game-scheduling" /> and an entrepreneurial approach to the widespread adoption of multiple listing for organ transplantation.<ref name="AtaSkaro2016" /><ref name="rothtayur" />

=== Books ===
[[File:MSOMHHA.jpg|thumb|A group of [[operations management]] scholars met to celebrate the Handbook of Healthcare Analytics at the 2017 MSOM Annual Meeting held at [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] (June 2017).]]
Tayur's co-edited volume, ''Quantitative Models for Supply Chain Management'' ([[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]], 1999), is among the most popular reference books on supply chain modeling.<ref>{{cite book|title=Quantitative Models for Supply Chain Management|publisher=Springer|year=1999|isbn=978-0-7923-8344-4|editor1-last=Tayur|editor1-first=S|editor2-last=Ganeshan|editor2-first=R|editor3-last=Magazine|editor3-first=M|url=https://archive.org/details/quantitativemode00srid}}</ref> Another, ''Handbook of Healthcare Analytics: Theoretical Minimum for Conducting 21st Century Research on Healthcare Operations'' ([[John Wiley & Sons]], 2018), covers a wide scope of contemporary topics and provides timely access to modern analytical tools;<ref>{{cite book|title=Handbook of Healthcare Analytics: Theoretical Minimum for Conducting 21st Century Research on Healthcare Operations|editor1-first=Tinglong|editor1-last=Dai|editor2-first=Sridhar|editor2-last=Tayur|year=2018|publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc.|isbn=978-1-119-30094-6|url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Handbook+of+Healthcare+Analytics%3A+Theoretical+Minimum+for+Conducting+21st+Century+Research+on+Healthcare+Operations-p-9781119300946}}</ref> the handbook is an "important volume" that "represents some of the brightest minds in analytics research, as well as physicians and senior healthcare executives."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cmu.edu/tepper/news/stories/2018/august/sridhar-tayur-handbook.html|title=Sridhar Tayur Publishes Comprehensive Handbook of Health Care Analytics – Tepper School of Business – Carnegie Mellon University|date=August 15, 2018|work=Tepper School of Business, Carnegie Mellon University|access-date=2018-08-15|language=en}}</ref>

=== Teaching ===
Tayur has won various undergraduate and MBA teaching awards, including the George Leland Bach Excellence in Teaching Award. One of Tayur's teaching cases, entitled “Managing Operations in the Time-Shared Jet Business," won First Prize for the INFORMS Teaching Case Award in 2000, and another, "Patient Experience Improvement at UPMC Eye Center," won Second Prize for the same award in 2012. In his chapter on "Operations Management MBA Teaching in 21st Century Business Schools,"<ref>{{Cite book|title=Cross-Functional Inventory Research|volume=10|last=Gavirneni|first=Srinagesh|publisher=World Scientific Publishing Co|year=2016|isbn=978-981-314-433-0|doi=10.1142/10148|series=World Scientific-Now Publishers Series in Business}}</ref> Tayur identifies five shared shortcomings between the “[[Harvard Business School|Harvard]] approach” (case study) and “[[Carnegie Mellon University|Carnegie]] approach” (mathematical models), suggesting a way to build on the best of both. He also notes entrepreneurship (including social enterprises) and the increased number of female MBAs as two important topics that need to be addressed more centrally in MBA education, with a goal of achieving the "higher aims" of management education beyond creating just another generation of "hired hands."[http://press.princeton.edu/titles/8463.html]

In collaboration with USRA/NASA and Amazon, and with NSF support, he developed a new course focused on Quantum Integer Programming (QuIP) in 2020,<ref>{{Cite web|title=47-779 – Quantum Integer Programming – CMU Fall 2020|url=https://bernalde.github.io/QuIP/|access-date=2021-10-30|website=bernalde.github.io}}</ref> and expanded it to include Quantum Machine Learning (QuML) in 2021.<ref name="QuML">{{Cite web|title=47-779/785 – Quantum Integer Programming and Quantum Machine Learning – CMU Fall 2021|url=https://bernalde.github.io/QuIPML/|access-date=2021-10-30|website=bernalde.github.io}}</ref>

Tayur has also taught in executive education programs for various companies, including [[McKinsey & Company]], [[Cisco Systems]], and [[Schibsted]].

=== Recognitions ===
Tayur was named one of the four “Masters of Supply-Chain Efficiency” by [[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune Magazine]],<ref name="tayurfortune">{{cite web|last=Siekman |first=Philip |url=https://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/2000/10/30/290626/index.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121216083244/http://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/2000/10/30/290626/index.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 16, 2012 |title=New Victories in the Supply-Chain Revolution Still looking for ways to tighten shipping, inventory, and even manufacturing costs at your company? Here's how four masters of supply-chain efficiency are doing it. – October 30, 2000 |publisher=Money.cnn.com |date=2000-10-30 |access-date=2012-09-09}}</ref> and a “Most Popular Professor” by [[Bloomberg Businessweek|BusinessWeek]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.businessweek.com/bschools/00/profiles/carnegiemellon.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001110085500/http://www.businessweek.com/bschools/00/profiles/carnegiemellon.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 10, 2000 |title=BW Online &#124; B-Schools |publisher=Businessweek.com |date=2000-08-01 |access-date=2012-09-09}}</ref> He has been ranked as one of the stellar operations management researchers.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://wpcarey.asu.edu/sites/default/files/uploads/journal-operations-management/essay5-howtodoresearch.pdf | author=Jiang, B. | title=How to do research: Advice from Stellar Scholars in the POM Field | publisher=Journal of Operations Management Forum | access-date=2015-05-11 | archive-date=2015-02-20 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150220013203/https://wpcarey.asu.edu/sites/default/files/uploads/journal-operations-management/essay5-howtodoresearch.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2012, Tayur was elected as a fellow of INFORMS for his lifetime achievements in “research on inventories and supply chain management, and developing new methodologies, implementing software in manufacturing, logistics and supply chains, and creating a market for enterprise [[inventory optimization]] software.” <ref name="informsfellow-tayur-informs">{{cite web| url=http://informs.org/Connect-with-People/Fellows/INFORMS-Fellows-Class-of-2012 | title= INFORMS Fellows: Class of 2012 | publisher=Informs.org | access-date=2012-10-10  }}</ref><ref group="note">The importance of inventory control to economic productivity has been widely recognized, including by the Nobel-winning economist [[Paul Krugman]], who states that, "The big productivity gains of the period from 1995 to 2005 came largely in things like inventory control" (See "[https://www.nytimes.com/2015/05/25/opinion/paul-krugman-the-big-meh.html The Big Meh]", by [[Paul Krugman]]).</ref>

In 2017, Tayur was elected as a Distinguished Fellow of MSOM. In the same year, he was elected as a Member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for "developing and commercializing innovative methods to optimize supply chain systems."<ref name="tayur-nae">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nae.edu/Projects/MediaRoom/20095/164396/165210.aspx|title=National Academy of Engineering Elects 84 Members and 22 Foreign Members|date=Feb 8, 2017|website=www.nae.edu|access-date=Feb 8, 2017}}</ref>

=== Awards ===
In the field of [[Healthcare]] Management, Tayur's paper "Imaging Room and Beyond: The Underlying Economics Behind Physicians’ Test-Ordering Behavior in Outpatient Services" won first place in the 2012 Production and Operations Management Society (POMS) College of Healthcare Operations Management's Best Paper Competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.poms.org/POMS%20Chronicle%20Vol%2019%20No%201.pdf |title=Healthcare Operations Management Best Paper Award |author= POMS |date= 2013 |publisher= Production and Operations Management Society | volume =19 |number=1 | access-date=15 December 2015}}</ref> In 2015, he won the Pierskalla Award for Best Paper in Healthcare from [[INFORMS]], for his paper, "OrganJet: Overcoming geographical disparities in access to deceased donor kidneys in the United States;"<ref>{{ cite web | url = https://www.informs.org/Recognize-Excellence/Community-Prizes-and-Awards/Health-Applications-Society/Pierskalla-Best-Paper-Award | title = Pierskalla Best Paper Award | date = 2015 | access-date = 15 December 2015 | author = Health Applications Society | publisher = INFORMS | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160513203612/https://www.informs.org/Recognize-Excellence/Community-Prizes-and-Awards/Health-Applications-Society/Pierskalla-Best-Paper-Award | archive-date = 13 May 2016 }}</ref> in 2019. The same paper was recognized as a finalist for the inaugural [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences|INFORMS]] MSOM Society's Award for Responsible Research in Operations Management.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/INFORMS/f779d040-38c8-42bb-aa09-0911d651a7eb/UploadedImages/Summer_2019_MSOM_Business_Meeting.pdf|title=Summer 2019 MSOM Society Business Meeting Minutes|website=INFORMS MSOM Society|access-date=August 4, 2019}}</ref> In 2021, his working paper titled "Toward a Liquid Biopsy: Greedy Approximation Algorithms for Active Sequential Hypothesis Testing" won the Pierskalla Award for Best Paper in Healthcare.<ref>{{Cite web|last=INFORMS|title=Pierskalla Best Paper Award|url=https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/Community-Prizes/Health-Applications-Society/Pierskalla-Best-Paper-Award|access-date=2021-10-30|website=INFORMS|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2022, he received the ''[[Manufacturing & Service Operations Management]]'' journal's Best Published Paper Award for his work on combating child labor in global supply chains.

His work with [[John Deere]]<ref name="tayur 05">{{cite journal |author1=L Troyer |author2=J Smith |author3=S Marshall |author4=E Yaniv |author5=S Tayur |author6=M Barkman |author7=A Kaya |author8=Y Liu |title = Improving Asset Management and Order Fulfillment at Deere & Company's C&CE Division| journal = Interfaces  | volume = 35 | issue = 1 | pages = 76–87  | year = 2005 | doi = 10.1287/inte.1040.0110|s2cid=16450411 }}</ref>—which reduced over $1B in inventory in just four years<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.supplychainquarterly.com/topics/Finance/scq200704deere/ | title= Running inventory like a Deere | author= James A. Cooke  | date = 2007 | issue = 4 | newspaper= Supply Chain Quarterly | access-date = July 2, 2015  }}</ref>—was a finalist for the [[Franz Edelman Award for Achievement in Operations Research and the Management Sciences|Edelman Prize]]. His PhD students have won a number of awards, including the [http://www.informs.org/Recognize-Excellence/INFORMS-Prizes-Awards/George-Nicholson-Student-Paper-Competition George Nicholson Prize in 1996] and the [http://www.informs.org/Recognize-Excellence/INFORMS-Prizes-Awards/George-B.-Dantzig-Dissertation-Award George B. Dantzig Dissertation Award] in 2011.

Tayur's work on [[integer programming]] using [[Gröbner basis]]<ref name=Tayur95>{{Cite journal | last1 = Tayur | first1 = S. R. | last2 = Thomas | first2 = R. R. | last3 = Natraj | first3 = N. R. | title = An algebraic geometry algorithm for scheduling in presence of setups and correlated demands | doi = 10.1007/BF01585566 | journal = Mathematical Programming | volume = 69 | issue = 1–3 | pages = 369–401 | year = 1995 | citeseerx = 10.1.1.41.7251 | s2cid = 18987327 }}</ref> was a finalist for the [[Frederick W. Lanchester Prize]].

In 2018, Tayur was chosen by [[Indian Institute of Technology Madras]] as a recipient of the 2018 Distinguished Alumni Awards (DAA).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/iit-madras-announces-distinguished-alumni-awards-2018/articleshow/62298270.cms|title=IIT-Madras announces Distinguished Alumni Awards 2018 – Times of India|work=The Times of India|access-date=2018-01-01}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Office of International & Alumni Affairs IIT Madras|title=IIT Madras – 59th Institute Day -26th april, 2018|date=2018-05-11|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrzAiDqLz7I&t=1h44m45s|access-date=2018-06-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://chennai36.iitm.ac.in/purpose-beyond-profit-dr-sridhar-tayur-daa-2018/|title=Purpose Beyond Profit- Dr. Sridhar R Tayur, DAA 2018 {{!}} Chennai36|website=chennai36.iitm.ac.in|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-08}}</ref>

== “Academic Capitalist” ==
As a serial entrepreneur and an active promoter of monetizing [[operations research]],<ref name="tayur interfaces 12">{{cite journal|doi=10.1287/inte.1100.0524|title = Editorial: How to Monetize the Value of OR|journal = Interfaces|volume = 40|issue = 6|pages = 446|year = 2010|last1 = Camm|first1 = Jeffrey D.|last2 = Tayur|first2 = Sridhar|doi-access = free}}</ref> Tayur coined the term “academic capitalist.”<ref name="rhsmithpdf">{{cite web|url=http://www.rhsmith.umd.edu/doit/msom2008/pdfs/abstractSridharTayur.pdf |title=An Academic Capitalist Reflects at Half-Time |date=5 June 2008 |publisher=rhsmith.umd.edu |access-date=9 September 2012 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317083043/http://www.rhsmith.umd.edu/doit/msom2008/pdfs/abstractSridharTayur.pdf |archive-date=March 17, 2012 }}</ref><ref name="stpomsdc15">{{cite web | url=http://pitt.hosted.panopto.com/Panopto/Pages/Viewer.aspx?id=e2b8d6d0-90c1-4f59-83a1-96b4ee47eb38 | title=Video of Sridhar Tayur's 2015 POMS Keynote Speech in Washington DC | date=May 2015 | access-date= May 27, 2015 | publisher=My PittVideo }}</ref><ref group="note">"Academic Capitalist" is similar to "Scientific Entrepreneur" (See "[https://www.amazon.com/The-Scientific-Life-History-Vocation/dp/0226750248 The Scientific Life; A moral history of a late modern vocation]", by [[Steven Shapin]]), and can be considered as a modern version of "craftsman-scholar" (See "[https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Lever_of_Riches.html?id=zo_8L4lT1z0C The Lever of Riches; Technological Creativity and Economic Progress]", by [[Joel Mokyr]]).</ref> Tayur is a charter member of The Indus Entrepreneurs ([[TiE]]),<ref name="tiecon">{{cite web| title= TiE StartupCon | url=http://tiestartupcon.com  | publisher= TiE | date=  May 2015|  access-date= May 10, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=TiE Pgh CM Table Talk: Sridhar Tayur| date=21 October 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3gazp2rO9iM|language=en|access-date=2019-10-28}}</ref> and has served as a mentor for TiE ScaleUp.<ref>{{Cite web|title = TiE ScaleUp – Splash|url = http://tiescaleup.splashthat.com|website = tiescaleup.splashthat.com|access-date = 2015-10-15}}</ref>

=== SmartOps ===
In 2000, Tayur founded the software company SmartOps Corporation, after winning the first prize in the EnterPrize Case Competition that year,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://old.post-gazette.com/businessnews/20000415enterprize3.asp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419013307/http://old.post-gazette.com/businessnews/20000415enterprize3.asp |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 19, 2014 | title=Very smart smartOps wins local competition | first=Ken | last=Zapinski | date=April 15, 2000 | newspaper = Pittsburgh Post-Gazette  }}</ref> and served as its CEO until 2012.

Through SmartOps, Tayur also coined the phrase "fix the mix" to refer to the approach of adjusting inventory levels for various items to meet target service levels with lower overall inventory investment.<ref>{{cite AV media |people= Sridhar Tayur |year= 2012 |title= Fix the Mix |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p6o5yHfDJ0Y |access-date=10 December 2013 |publisher=SmartOpsFilms }}</ref> Several SmartOps customers, including [[Cabot Corporation]], [[Celestica]],<ref>{{cite AV media |people= Luciano Miranda |year= 2013 |title= Customer Story: Celestica – Inventory Planning and Optimization Forum 2012 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4AcjAfWBVXg&feature=c4-overview-vl&list=PL-ugJq8UjMGn2t80T64ves-O1OclrsWrK |access-date=10 December 2013 |publisher=SmartOpsFilms }}</ref> [[ConAgra]], [[Dow Chemical Company]], [[Johnson & Johnson]],<ref>{{cite AV media |people= Tony Verbeck |year= 2013 |title= Supply Chain Digest – Johnson & Johnson – Tony Verbeck |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XFM67FQyzNk |access-date=10 December 2013 |publisher=SmartOpsFilms }}</ref> [[Kohler Company]], [[Lubrizol]], [[LSI Corporation]], [[Medtronic]], [[PPG Industries]],<ref>{{cite AV media |people= Peter Ten Hagen |year= 2013 |title= Customer Story: PPG Industries – Inventory Planning & Optimization Forum 2012 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=txAFQrjoR_w |access-date=10 December 2013 |publisher=SmartOpsFilms }}</ref> [[Wyeth]], have spoken about their successes with Enterprise Inventory Optimization (EIO).

SmartOps was in a revenue sharing contract agreement with [[SAP AG]], until February 2013, when SAP AG announced that it would acquire SmartOps to develop a real-time supply chain software that allows its customers to "run their businesses in real time—to analyze, predict, react and adjust instantly."<ref name="sap-acq">{{cite news | url=http://www.news-sap.com/sap-acquires-smartops-to-help-customers-optimize-inventory-and-service-levels-in-supply-chain/ | title=SAP Acquires SmartOps to Help Customers Optimize Inventory and Service Levels in Supply Chain | date= February 22, 2013 | newspaper= SAP Newsroom  }}</ref><ref name="info-age-smartops">{{cite news | url=http://www.information-age.com/industry/software/123456832/sap-buys--stochastic--supply-chain-specialist-smartops | first= Pete  | last= Swabey | title=SAP buys "stochastic" supply chain specialist SmartOps | date= February 25, 2013 | newspaper = Information Age  }}</ref><ref name="pitt-smartops-sap">{{cite news | url= http://www.bizjournals.com/pittsburgh/blog/innovation/2013/02/sap-picks-up-smartops-to-boost.html | first=Malia| last=Spencer | title=SAP picks up SmartOps to boost real-time enterprise management | date= February 25, 2013| newspaper=Pittsburgh Business Times  }}</ref> Through this acquisition, SAP was able to offer an integrated [[inventory management software]], allowing its clients to "manage the increased supply chain risk due to economic uncertainty, escalating customer expectations, demand volatility, and supply variability they face."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wiki.scn.sap.com/wiki/display/SCM/SAP+Integrated+Business+Planning+for+Inventory|title=SAP Integrated Business Planning for Inventory – Supply Chain Management (SCM) – SCN Wiki|last=Ghita|first=Alecsandra|date=Nov 17, 2016|website=wiki.scn.sap.com|access-date=2017-03-03}}</ref>

Tayur has been recognized for his entrepreneurship of SmartOps Corporation by the [[Carnegie Science Center]] Award for Innovation in Information Technology,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/local/uncategorized/heroes-honored-as-07-science-center-award-recipients-470370/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140118061216/http://www.post-gazette.com/frontpage/2007/02/01/Heroes-honored-as-07-Science-Center-award-recipients/stories/200702010544|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 18, 2014|title='Heroes' honored as '07 Science Center award recipients|last=Templeton|first=David|date=Feb 1, 2007|newspaper=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette}}</ref> and has been the subject of [[University of Virginia Darden School of Business]]'s MBA Teaching case “SmartOps Corporation: Forging Smart Alliances?”<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cb.hbsp.harvard.edu/cbmp/product/UV5755-PDF-ENG|title=SmartOps Corporation: Forging Smart Alliances?|publisher=Harvard Business Publishing|access-date=9 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.coursera.org/lecture/uva-darden-bcg-pricing-strategy-market-competition/case-debrief-smartops-nQAgW|title=Case Debrief: SmartOps – Disrupting Markets and Engaging in "Coopetition"|website=Coursera|language=en|access-date=2020-02-10}}</ref>

=== OrganJet and GuardianWings ===
In 2011, Tayur founded the [[social enterprise]] OrganJet Corporation, which facilities multiple listings and provides on-demand private jet transportation for patients to receive [[organ transplantation]] in a wider geographic range.<ref>{{cite news | first=Julie | last=Cohn | url=http://www.thedaily.com/page/2012/06/03/060312-biz-organjet-cohn-1-4|title=Angel of the Airways: OrganJet matches patients to life-saving flights for transplants| date=June 3, 2012 | newspaper=The Daily}}</ref><ref name="rothtayur">{{cite web|url=https://marketdesigner.blogspot.com/2012/10/sridhar-tayur-proposes-entrepreneurial.html |title=Sridhar Tayur proposes an entrepreneurial way to reform organ waiting lists | author = Roth, Alvin |author-link= Alvin E. Roth | work= Market Design | date = October 24, 2012 | access-date=December 13, 2012 }}</ref> Since the founding of OrganJet, Tayur's "entrepreneurial approach to reform [the] organ waiting list" has caught the attention of Nobel Laureate [[Alvin E. Roth]], among other preeminent economists.<ref name="rothtayur" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://marketdesigner.blogspot.com/search?q=organjet|title=Organjet versus regional transplant lists|last=Roth|first=Alvin E.|date=August 31, 2014|access-date=November 12, 2014}}</ref> In addition, OrganJet has been covered by the AOL/MAKERS initiative<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.makers.com/katharine-wolf | title=KATHARINE WOLF, Social Challenge Advisor | access-date= 18 May 2015 }}</ref> and by the media in regions suffering from geographic disparity in waiting times for organ transplants, such as Boston,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2014/09/29/i-team-professor-helps-organ-transplant-patients-on-multiple-waiting-lists | title=I-Team: Professor Helps Organ Transplant Patients On Multiple Waiting Lists |last=Leamanczyk|first=Lauren |publisher=WBZ-TV | date=Nov 29, 2014 | access-date=Nov 30, 2014 }}</ref> Denver,<ref name="oj-denver">{{cite news | url=http://denver.cbslocal.com/2014/10/27/transplant-wait-times-longer-in-colorado-than-surrounding-states/| title=Transplant Wait Times Longer in Colorado than Surrounding States | date=October 27, 2014 | access-date=October 28, 2014   |newspaper=CBS Denver }}</ref> and Wisconsin.<ref>{{cite news | url= http://host.madison.com/news/local/health_med_fit/access-to-liver-transplants-unequal-in-wisconsin-nation/article_c5067967-7e0c-5307-b591-78f2d62648bd.html#.VVx3OGQ2TXo.email | title=Access to liver transplants unequal in Wisconsin, nation | newspaper=Wisconsin State Journal | date = May 11, 2015 | access-date = May 20, 2015 | first=David | last= Wahlberg  }}</ref>

In July 2012, with the founding of GuardianWings, Tayur became the first [[social entrepreneurship|social entrepreneur]] to start a “contract hybrid,” in which a for-profit entity (OrganJet) is symbiotically integrated with a not-for-profit subsidiary (GuardianWings) sharing a common social mission of providing inclusive access to [[organ transplantation]].
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O6Z6k6RF434|title=Life Saver: Sridhar Tayur's OrganJet|date=17 December 2012 |publisher=youtube.com|access-date=8 February 2013}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bio-itworld.com/2012/10/19/can-private-jets-for-poor-save-health-care-dollars.html|title=Can Private Jets For The Poor Save Health Care Dollars?|publisher=bio-itworld.com|access-date=22 October 2012}}</ref><ref group="note">The notion of “contract hybrids,” as a new legal entity, was first proposed by [http://www.ssireview.org/images/articles/2011SP_Feature_Bromberger.pdf Bromberger (2011)] as a method to obtain the best of “for-profit” and “not-for-profit” entities, and further explored by [http://www.ssireview.org/pdf/Summer_2012_In_Search_of_the_Hybrid_Ideal.pdf Battilana et al. (2012)]</ref> A 2013 [[Harvard Business School]] case titled "OrganJet and GuardianWings" (by [[Julie Battilana]] and James Weber), covering the decision process behind the organizational structure of OrganJet and GuardianWings,<ref name="hbs-organjet" /> has been taught at [[Harvard Business School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://instructionalmoves.gse.harvard.edu/julie-battilana|title=Julie Battilana|website=instructionalmoves.gse.harvard.edu|language=en|access-date=2020-01-21}}</ref> The case has also been used by the [[University of Michigan]]'s [[Ross School of Business]], among other business schools, in its course "The Corporation in Society," where Tayur was interviewed by the instructor Jim Walsh.<ref>{{cite AV media|url=http://www.bus.umich.edu/Video/Play/new.asp?file=Ross/SridharTayur-Interview|title=An Interview with Sridhar Tayur|people=Sridhar Tayur and James Walsh|publisher=Umich.edu|year=2013|access-date=13 November 2013}}</ref> Students were asked to write responses to the question "If you were Sridhar Tayur, how do you think about your aspirations to establish OrganJet and GuardianWings, change the current transplant system in America, honor your commitments to Carnegie-Mellon University, and live a full life?" <ref>{{cite web|url=http://jamespwalsh.com/Resources/Strategy%20411%20--%20The%20Corporation%20in%20Society--%20Fall%202013.pdf|title=The Corporation in Society (Strategy 411, Fall 2013)|author=Walsh, James|publisher=Jamespwalsh.com|access-date=13 November 2013}}</ref> In an interview with [[The Guardian]], Tayur said that the hybrid model was more efficient than a traditional pure for-profit or not-for-profit: "It would have been much easier for me to have said it's a not-for-profit or a for-profit and satisfy the skeptics. But the primary goal of my company is to help as many people as possible get transplants quicker."<ref name="tg-st">{{cite news|last=Alison|first=Moodie|date=21 November 2013|title=The NGO-Business Hybrid: More Than the Sum of Its Parts? (Case Study: OrganJet)|newspaper=The Guardian|location=London|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sustainable-business/interactive/business-structures-sustainability-connection-interactive|access-date=26 November 2013}}</ref>

On August 7, 2013, it was announced that Irena Bucci, a resident of the Washington D.C. area, successfully received a kidney transplant in Pittsburgh through the service provided by OrganJet.<ref name="dc-resident-oj">{{cite news|url=http://www.transplantsnews.com/being-an-organ-recipient/multiple-listing-to-reduce-wait-times-for-transplant-patients |title=Multiple Listing to Reduce Wait Times for Transplant Patients | newspaper= Transplant News | date = June 13, 2014 | access-date=June 13, 2014 }}</ref> In June 2014, OrganJet sponsored a “Transplants” campaign with Mediaplanet and [[USA Today]] aiming to increase the public's awareness of the importance of organ donation.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.prweb.com/releases/mediaplanet_launches_transplants_campaign_inspiring_americans_to_take_action/prweb11941887.htm | title=Mediaplanet Launches "Transplants" Campaign Inspiring Americans to Take Action | date = June 13, 2014 | access-date=June 13, 2014   }}</ref> On August 20, 2013, OrganJet released a free self-service [[Application software|App]] to help [[chronic kidney disease]] patients find a low wait kidney transplant center in the US.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.laptopmag.com/organjet-finds-kidneys | title=Need a Kidney? There's an App for That | author=Andronico, Michael | work=LAPTOP | date=Aug 20, 2013 | access-date=Aug 25, 2013 }}</ref>
[[File:Tayur-Sen-HS.jpg|thumb|Tayur with [[Amartya Sen]] at [[Harvard Square]] (May 2016)]]

A 2014 piece in ''[[The Atlantic]],'' "A Private Jet Is Waiting to Take You to Your Kidney Transplant" detailed Tayur's motivation behind founding OrganJet and the company's latest developments.<ref name="tayur-atlantic">{{cite news | url=https://www.theatlantic.com/health/archive/2014/10/the-businessman-disrupting-organ-transplantation/381843/?single_page=true | title=A Private Jet Is Waiting to Take You to Your Kidney Transplant | last=Lamas|first=Daniela | newspaper= The Atlantic | date=Oct 29, 2014 | access-date=Oct 29, 2014 }}</ref> In discussing geographic inequality in organ transplantation, a 2014 ''[[The New England Journal of Medicine]]'' article cited OrganJet as an example of mobilizing the recipients (instead of mobilizing the organs) that would face less of the "political resistance that has stood in the way of broader organ sharing to date."<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1056/NEJMp1407639| pmid = 25539104| title = Transplantation Traffic – Geography as Destiny for Transplant Candidates| journal = New England Journal of Medicine| volume = 371| issue = 26| pages = 2450–2| year = 2014| last1 = Ubel | first1 = P. A. }}</ref> The ''[[American Journal of Transplantation]]'', in its February 2015 issue of "The AJT Report," mentioned Tayur and his work through OrganJet as one of "grassroots groups and organizations formed to improve the quality of life for transplant candidates, recipients, their families, and the families of organ and tissue donors."<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1111/ajt.13209| pmid = 25612479| title = TheAJTReport| journal = American Journal of Transplantation| volume = 15| issue = 2| pages = 291–2| year = 2015| last1 = Pondrom| first1 = S| doi-access = free}}</ref> Tayur and OrganJet have also been profiled in ''The Craft of Creativity'',<ref name="CroninLoewenstein2018" />'' [[Ars Technica]]'',<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://arstechnica.com/science/2017/03/live-death-math-and-efficiency-the-quest-to-solve-us-organ-transplants-woes/2/|title=Steve Jobs' liver—and the quest for a better organ algorithm|work=Ars Technica|access-date=2017-03-16|language=en-us}}</ref> ''[[Forbes]]'',<ref>{{cite news | url 29 June 2015 | access-date = 1 July 2015 |newspaper = Forbes  }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url =https://www.forbes.com/sites/peterubel/2015/06/30/your-new-liver-is-only-a-learjet-away-part-3-of-3/  |
